#### 5.10.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** desynchronization, unbounded history, ambiguous rewind interface. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `ghost projected shadows preview future positions; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/future-shadow/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/future-shadow/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/future-shadow/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 11. Bellflower Cavern — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G11`)
**Source:** `G220`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.56 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Strike floating bells in sequence to open procedural caves. **Signature animated environment:** glowing radial sound ripples bloom across mineral walls; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals. **Core abstraction:** pulse propagation graph.
#### 5.11.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees glowing radial sound ripples bloom across mineral walls; instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Strike floating bells in sequence to open procedural caves. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `pulse propagation graph` computational rules, visual `glowing radial sound ripples bloom across mineral walls; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals` and player control arrangement `Position/trigger resonators and infer hidden 3D structure`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.11.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** arrival_time(x)=||x-source||/c with bounded distance field and quantized pulse ticks. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Strike floating bells in sequence to open procedural caves. Normalize input into `BellflowerCavernAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place emitters so returning wavefronts reveal an ordered signal pattern. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 5 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** discrete emitter search with exact arrival-order and occlusion checks. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** misleading sound analogy, ring overdraw and strobe risk. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.11.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting glowing radial sound ripples bloom across mineral walls; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable pulse propagation graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with strike floating bells in sequence to open procedural caves; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative pulse propagation graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Position/trigger resonators and infer hidden 3D structure. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.11.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** expanding ring meshes, volumetric-look pulse shells and glowing distance bands. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** glowing radial sound ripples bloom across mineral walls; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `BellflowerCavernScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `BellflowerCavernParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `1bafe4654754` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.11.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 12. Petal Palace — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G12`)
**Source:** `G312`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.54 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Close and unfold radial walls to route visitors represented by light points. **Signature animated environment:** pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. **Core abstraction:** room hinge graph.
#### 5.12.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Close and unfold radial walls to route visitors represented by light points. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `room hinge graph` computational rules, visual `pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` and player control arrangement `Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.12.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** world transforms of connected panels rotate around shared manifold hinges. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Close and unfold radial walls to route visitors represented by light points. Normalize input into `PetalPalaceAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** hinge-state graph search plus reachability and collision certificates. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.12.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable room hinge graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with close and unfold radial walls to route visitors represented by light points; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative room hinge graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.12.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `PetalPalaceScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `PetalPalaceParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `fa00c4267999` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.12.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.12.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `pleated shell roofs bloom like mechanical flowers; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/petal-palace/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/petal-palace/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/petal-palace/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. **Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 13. Tessera Passage — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G13`)
**Source:** `G314`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.53 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Flip triangular platforms to connect a route across voids. **Signature animated environment:** geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. **Core abstraction:** room hinge graph.
#### 5.13.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Flip triangular platforms to connect a route across voids. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `room hinge graph` computational rules, visual `geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` and player control arrangement `Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.13.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** world transforms of connected panels rotate around shared manifold hinges. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Flip triangular platforms to connect a route across voids. Normalize input into `TesseraPassageAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** hinge-state graph search plus reachability and collision certificates. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.13.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable room hinge graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with flip triangular platforms to connect a route across voids; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative room hinge graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.13.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `TesseraPassageScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `TesseraPassageParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `b4968d45d8cb` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.13.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.13.10. Cross-model render, endurance, abnormal state and deterministic fault-injection matrix

#### 5.13.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `geometric tiling reorients luminous portals; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/tessera-passage/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/tessera-passage/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/tessera-passage/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 14. Looped Waterfall — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G14`)
**Source:** `G444`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.53 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Change time offsets to bring waterfall drops into matching sockets. **Signature animated environment:** sparkling reverse-flow ribbons suspended among stone ledges; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders. **Core abstraction:** fixed-step timeline.
#### 5.14.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees sparkling reverse-flow ribbons suspended among stone ledges; deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Change time offsets to bring waterfall drops into matching sockets. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `fixed-step timeline` computational rules, visual `sparkling reverse-flow ribbons suspended among stone ledges; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders` and player control arrangement `Edit events in a short loop to produce a future alignment`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.14.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** state[k+1]=F(state[k],actions[k]); snapshot every 120 ticks and hash canonical state. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Change time offsets to bring waterfall drops into matching sockets. Normalize input into `LoopedWaterfallAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** synchronize target events at the same integer tick without invalid contacts. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded time-expanded search with cycle memoization. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** desynchronization, unbounded history, ambiguous rewind interface. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.14.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting sparkling reverse-flow ribbons suspended among stone ledges; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable fixed-step timeline handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with change time offsets to bring waterfall drops into matching sockets; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative fixed-step timeline predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Edit events in a short loop to produce a future alignment. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.14.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** motion trails, reversible shader deformation and ghost snapshots. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** sparkling reverse-flow ribbons suspended among stone ledges; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `LoopedWaterfallScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `LoopedWaterfallParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `25828ef2cb01` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.14.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct fixed-step timeline controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 15. Iris Cascade — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G15`)
**Source:** `G404`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.52 /100**, proposed upfront price **$2.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Control an iris aperture chain to pass a precise sequence of colored pulses. **Signature animated environment:** opening petals and bright traveling beams; GLSL hue transforms, procedural glass polygons, spline light tubes and glow. **Core abstraction:** spectral constraint grid.
#### 5.15.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees opening petals and bright traveling beams; glsl hue transforms, procedural glass polygons, spline light tubes and glow, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Control an iris aperture chain to pass a precise sequence of colored pulses. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `spectral constraint grid` computational rules, visual `opening petals and bright traveling beams; GLSL hue transforms, procedural glass polygons, spline light tubes and glow` and player control arrangement `Match spectral state in 3D without conflicting colors`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.15.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** discrete hue index h in Z_12; edge transfer h_next=(h+δ) mod 12; secondary glyph code. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Control an iris aperture chain to pass a precise sequence of colored pulses. Normalize input into `IrisCascadeAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** satisfy a target spectral pattern subject to unique-neighbor exclusion constraints. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** constraint propagation + backtracking with uniqueness proof. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** accessibility, near-similar hues, fake additive mixing rules. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.15.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting opening petals and bright traveling beams; GLSL hue transforms, procedural glass polygons, spline light tubes and glow; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable spectral constraint grid handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with control an iris aperture chain to pass a precise sequence of colored pulses; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative spectral constraint grid predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Match spectral state in 3D without conflicting colors. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.15.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** GLSL color wheel, translucent solids and emissive edge tubes. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** opening petals and bright traveling beams; GLSL hue transforms, procedural glass polygons, spline light tubes and glow. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `IrisCascadeScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `IrisCascadeParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `c5bf59d2352b` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.15.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct spectral constraint grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 16. Hypercube Windows — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G16`)
**Source:** `G436`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.52 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Rotate projections of a four-dimensional object to find a 3D path. **Signature animated environment:** hypercube projection lines and luminous depth cues; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. **Core abstraction:** hinged face net.
#### 5.16.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees hypercube projection lines and luminous depth cues; reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Rotate projections of a four-dimensional object to find a 3D path. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `hinged face net` computational rules, visual `hypercube projection lines and luminous depth cues; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials` and player control arrangement `Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.16.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** R_i(θ_i) transforms adjacent faces around shared edge; reject 3D triangle intersections. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Rotate projections of a four-dimensional object to find a 3D path. Normalize input into `HypercubeWindowsAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** fold a legal geometric net into a connected target solid without self-collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over discretized hinge states with swept triangle intersection. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** folding singularities, Z-fighting, hidden face gestures. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.16.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting hypercube projection lines and luminous depth cues; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable hinged face net handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with rotate projections of a four-dimensional object to find a 3d path; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative hinged face net predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.16.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted polyhedron mesh, glowing seams and easing hinge transforms. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** hypercube projection lines and luminous depth cues; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `HypercubeWindowsScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `HypercubeWindowsParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `dfbd9bc297ed` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.16.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.
