#### 5.23.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `analytic water caustics race across stepped marble and glass vaults; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/caustic-courtyard/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/caustic-courtyard/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/caustic-courtyard/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 24. Photon Loom — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G24`)
**Source:** `G208`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.42 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Cross filaments of light through three-dimensional knots without tangling them. **Signature animated environment:** glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. **Core abstraction:** ray/wave optical graph.
#### 5.24.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, sdf optics and gradient materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Cross filaments of light through three-dimensional knots without tangling them. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `ray/wave optical graph` computational rules, visual `glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` and player control arrangement `Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.24.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Cross filaments of light through three-dimensional knots without tangling them. Normalize input into `PhotonLoomAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** route or phase-align rays through specified optical stations. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded ray graph traversal with plane intersections and reflection/refraction validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.24.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable ray/wave optical graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with cross filaments of light through three-dimensional knots without tangling them; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative ray/wave optical graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.24.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** projected caustics, beam cylinders, chromatic dispersion approximations. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `PhotonLoomScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `PhotonLoomParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `e052b179fa16` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.24.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.24.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `glowing ray strands and moving interference ribbons; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/photon-loom/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/photon-loom/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/photon-loom/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 25. Stardust Weaver — complete proposed implementation design (`R05-G25`)
**Source:** `G382`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.42 /100**, proposed upfront price **$2.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Draw attraction fields that braid star dust into luminous ribbons. **Signature animated environment:** dense sparkling 3D filaments and trail decay; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes. **Core abstraction:** bounded field integrator.
#### 5.25.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees dense sparkling 3d filaments and trail decay; batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Draw attraction fields that braid star dust into luminous ribbons. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `bounded field integrator` computational rules, visual `dense sparkling 3D filaments and trail decay; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes` and player control arrangement `Shepherd particle clusters through spatial constraints`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.25.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** v+=a(x,t)Δt; x+=vΔt, fixed step; stable particle IDs and bounded occupancy. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Draw attraction fields that braid star dust into luminous ribbons. Normalize input into `StardustWeaverAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** steer clusters into target regions while avoiding forbidden regions. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 5 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** sampled state-space field-controller search and cluster membership proof. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** particle overdraw, thermals on D3, non-deterministic GPU sorting. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.25.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting dense sparkling 3D filaments and trail decay; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable bounded field integrator handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with draw attraction fields that braid star dust into luminous ribbons; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative bounded field integrator predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Shepherd particle clusters through spatial constraints. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.25.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** GL_POINT sprites, instanced halos, fade trails and glow compositing. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** dense sparkling 3D filaments and trail decay; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `StardustWeaverScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `StardustWeaverParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `d115cabff7f8` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.25.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.25.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** particle overdraw, thermals on D3, non-deterministic GPU sorting. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `dense sparkling 3D filaments and trail decay; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/stardust-weaver/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/stardust-weaver/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND5_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round5/stardust-weaver/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

## 6. Complete Claim–Reason–Evidence AssertionOutlines for all 25 proposed games
Each argument is an INVESTMENT HYPOTHESIS. Claims are contestable. Each of three claims has four reasons and exactly one specific evidence basis. "Proposed verification" means future evidence to collect, not an already observed success; "published comparable" is evidence of the category, NOT of demand for this proposed app. Counterarguments are not suppressed.
### Argument 01: Shadow Mosaic
#### Claim 1 — Shadow Mosaic is worth prototyping as a visually differentiated one-price mobile game because fill a target silhouette with overlapping projected 3d solids.
- **Reason 1:** The player has an identifiable and testable decision: Fill a target silhouette with overlapping projected 3D solids.
  - **Evidence 1.1 (type identified):** Specific instance: proposed first-session tutorial and `arrange solids so projected shadows form a required shape or route` pass/fail contract.
- **Reason 2:** The world has a strong immediate visual signature: geometric shadow cutouts morph between recognizable motifs; Procedural solids, CPU polygonal 3D shadow projections, soft shadow approximation.
  - **Evidence 1.2 (type identified):** Specific instance: shader recipe `CPU-projected analytic soft shadow stencil with light shaft geometry` with deterministic camera and seed to capture later.
- **Reason 3:** The genre has public commercial precedents, but not a guaranteed market.
  - **Evidence 1.3 (type identified):** Public comparable: [Baba Is You official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/736260/Baba_Is_You/) is a genre reference; it does NOT demonstrate this proposal’s sales.
- **Reason 4:** Completeness avoids the empty graphics-demo problem.
  - **Evidence 1.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: 100 certified levels, genuine solver witnesses and XCUITest win/loss/undo acceptance for `Shadow Mosaic`.
#### Claim 2 — Shadow Mosaic is a credible code-only VisualCore production because the core aesthetic, geometric shadow cutouts morph between recognizable motifs; procedural solids, cpu polygonal 3d shadow projections, soft shadow approximation, can be built with deterministic shaders and meshes.
- **Reason 1:** The projective shadow geometry simulation has mathematical semantics independent of textures.
  - **Evidence 2.1 (type identified):** Method/design evidence: `shadow mask=∪Π_light(occluder solids), compare raster IoU and Hausdorff boundary` defines numeric truth; CPU-only unit tests will verify results.
- **Reason 2:** Procedural assets can offer many visual compositions without artists.
  - **Evidence 2.2 (type identified):** Method/design evidence: game seed, mesh compiler, shader parameters and `geometric shadow cutouts morph between recognizable motifs; Procedural solids, CPU polygonal 3D shadow projections, soft shadow approximation` vary under bounded deterministic controls.
- **Reason 3:** The renderer is a known reusable abstraction rather than twenty-five unrelated engines.
  - **Evidence 2.3 (type identified):** Engineering reference: ProjectM-iOS ANGLE/Metal is publicly documented; validate VisualCore local public adapter before implementation.
- **Reason 4:** Visual beauty will be measured in actual frames, not promotional mockups.
  - **Evidence 2.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: actual GL screenshot goldens, shader compilation logs and D3 endurance for `Shadow Mosaic`.
#### Claim 3 — Shadow Mosaic is worth an evidence-gated paid release because its puzzle completeness, device performance and market identity can be tested and falsified before publication.
- **Reason 1:** Commercial risk is bounded by a compact unique core loop.
  - **Evidence 3.1 (type identified):** Design instance: `Fill a target silhouette with overlapping projected 3D solids` and `arrange solids so projected shadows form a required shape or route` define a concise standalone paid product.
- **Reason 2:** The implementation can be stopped honestly if gameplay is unconvincing.
  - **Evidence 3.2 (type identified):** Proposed falsifier: failing tutorial clarity, engagement test or original-product comparison triggers PIVOT or NO_GO.
- **Reason 3:** The recorded hardware set enables controlled performance decisions.
  - **Evidence 3.3 (type identified):** Owner-supplied devices.md: D1 iPhone15,4; D2 iPad17,3; D3 iPad15,7 on iPadOS 26.5—no results claimed.
- **Reason 4:** A real code-only app avoids the cost and licensing risks of image-generation assets.
  - **Evidence 3.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: grep dependencies and compiled binary for network/art SDKs; zero manual hero-image files; source-level procedural appearance `CPU-projected analytic soft shadow stencil with light shaft geometry`.
**Counterargument:** Shadow Mosaic may be a visually appealing but commercially weak shader toy; `shadow self-intersection, ambiguous depth, darkness hides interactions` may also defeat the D3 performance budget. An analogy is not evidence of demand, and no simulated metrics substitute for hardware. **Response/experiment:** show a complete 3-minute new-user win with no assistance, audit all 100 solver witnesses, capture real iOS rendered frames, collect third-party comprehension feedback, compare against existing apps for originality, and reject paid release if actual evidence is weak.
**Decision:** CONSIDER only after all real seed/solver/simulator/device checks; PIVOT if visual readability or originality fails; COMBINE if another title shares the same core goal; NO_GO if D3 cannot sustain a viable quality tier or the product is not enjoyable.

## 7. Full implementation → simulator → device sequential execution protocol
| Gate ID | Exact action | Exit evidence | Device allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R05-PREFLIGHT` | Independent previous round4 completed audit and source/skills discovery | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R05-SHARED` | 12 shared features fully specified, implemented and converged; final audit F12 can be deferred to post-device | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R05-GAME` | 25 apps × ten subfeatures fully converged and documented, no placeholders | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R05-SIM` | 25 real targets compiling and all unit, shader and simulator acceptance executed | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R05-LOCK` | Generate verified source SHA, binary catalog, simulator logs, test plan and proof manifests | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test until verified |
| `R05-D1` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D1; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D1 only |
| `R05-D2` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D2; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D2 only |
| `R05-D3` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D3; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D3 only, NEVER UPDATE |
| `R05-AUDIT` | Converge shared F12, reconcile regressions and final no-ads/legal/graphics audit | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | Only targeted retests after three runs |

On every Desktop session: verify real prior-round manifests and source hashes, acquire atomic file lease, inspect git SHA, select first dependency-ready task, invoke installed Spec Kit skills one at a time, inspect produced artifacts, run independent real tests, fsync+os.replace evidence ledger, commit reviewed changes, and prepare accurate next-action prompt. Never ask a Python script to call Claude CLI or private model APIs. The desktop app may pause for usage/tool prompts; never claim continuous execution when it was interrupted.
**Bounded-context retrieval:** Every round file is multiple megabytes. Use a Python heading index, then fetch only the current feature heading, its complete eight prompts, and directly cited contracts. Never load all prior rounds or all commands into a single Claude conversation. Persist feature heading offsets, SHA-256 and next-action cursor in .autonomy state. A truncated snippet is not a completed reading of a feature.
### 7.2 Deterministic host/simulator/device shell commands (agent runs via Terminal tool, not Claude CLI)
```bash
set -euo pipefail
git rev-parse HEAD; git status --short
specify --help; specify integration list
find .claude/skills -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md -print
xcodebuild -version; xcrun simctl list devices available -j
python3 scripts/verify_environment.py # if existing from previous rounds
python3 scripts/check_compliance.py # if existing; otherwise implement compatible audit
xcodegen generate # after additive project.yml changes and validation
python3 Tools/python/round5_preflight.py --previous round4.md --strict
python3 Tools/python/round5_generate_levels.py --all --check-solver --verify-hashes
python3 Tools/python/round5_simulators.py --all --runtimes 26.5,27.2 --result-bundle-dir docs/test-reports/round5/simulator/
python3 Tools/python/round5_feature_ledger.py lock --require-complete-simulator-evidence
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output /tmp/round-devices.json
python3 Tools/python/round5_devices.py --device D1 --all --require-lock --automation-build --results docs/test-reports/round5/D1/
python3 Tools/python/round5_devices.py --device D2 --all --require-lock --automation-build --results docs/test-reports/round5/D2/
python3 Tools/python/round5_devices.py --device D3 --all --require-lock --automation-build --results docs/test-reports/round5/D3/
python3 Tools/python/round5_collect_evidence.py --all --validate --hash
python3 Tools/python/round5_audit.py --all --device-evidence-required --no-ads --code-only --originality
```
These are **expected script names and interfaces to IMPLEMENT**, not commands falsely claimed to work today. Validate all installed tool versions, simulator runtime availability and Apple `devicectl` syntax before invocation. Android, Linux, and Windows graphics performance cannot be inferred from iOS simulator results. Device trust/signing requires owner provisioning.

### 7.3 Actual devicectl and XCTest building blocks (only AFTER implementation lock)
```bash
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output /tmp/visualcore-round-devices.json
# Resolve D1/D2/D3 by hardwareProperties.productType and current OS/build, not array position
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "${DEVICE_IDENTIFIER}" "${SIGNED_AUTOMATION_APP}"
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "${DEVICE_IDENTIFIER}" --terminate-existing --environment-variables '{"ROUND5_AUTORUN":"win_replay"}' "${BUNDLE_ID}"
xcrun devicectl device info files --device "${DEVICE_IDENTIFIER}" --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier "${BUNDLE_ID}" --subdirectory Documents --json-output /tmp/appfiles.json
xcrun devicectl device copy from --device "${DEVICE_IDENTIFIER}" --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier "${BUNDLE_ID}" --source Documents/automation-result.json --destination "${EVIDENCE_DIR}/automation-result.json"
xcodebuild test -project "${PROJECT_PATH}" -scheme "${SCHEME}" -destination "platform=iOS,id=${HARDWARE_UDID}" -resultBundlePath "${RESULT_BUNDLE}" -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180
```
Verify the real installed `devicectl --help` syntax before driving the machine. A device runner must detect locked or untrusted devices, use actual hardware UDIDs for XCTest, quote arguments, redact credentials, keep a maximum runtime, export bounded JSON reports, and terminate each launch mode. Apple signing and trust are owner-controlled. In shipping Release, verify via `nm -U` and build flags that all automation symbols are absent. Never mark a device test passed from a simulator.

Every planned sample row must become a real unique record (with actual start/end date and device) before any VERIFIED_DEVICE flag. 200 sample runs needed for a percentage metric when such a claim is made; speculative 60fps/30min are engineering goals, not facts. Mean/median/p95 require sample counts and warm/cold separation. First install may need onboarding; actual measurements begin only after explicit ready state. Shipping Release compiled without automation symbols (`nm -U` check). Device `hardwareProperties.udid` differs from some devicectl ID fields; resolve consistently. Physical owner operations like unlock, trust and first microphone permissions are unautomatable without prior setup.
### 9.1 Expected CI stages
- **docs-compliance:** validate specs, IDs, no-ad-art privacy policy and metadata. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **swift-host:** SwiftPM rule/solver/replay tests on host. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **linux-foundations:** where dependencies permit, compile CPU-only math packages on Linux. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **native-xcframeworks:** cache pinned projectM + ANGLE frameworks by exact source SHA and Xcode build. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **ios26-simulator:** all 25 apps compile/test and run fallback code paths on iOS 26.5. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **ios27-simulator:** all 25 apps compile/test on iOS 27.2 and available capture guards. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **full-visual-regression:** render actual seeded scenes, record shader compile and compare baselines. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.
- **package-and-audit:** artifact hashes, deterministic content, privacy/license/ad/no-images gates. Set explicit CI timeout, cancellation policy, restricted write permissions and distinguish Mac-only jobs. Do not assume GitHub runner availability without checking current product/toolchain.

<!-- BEGIN VERBATIM 500-GAME STUDY REFERENCE -->
# VisualCore Premium 3D Games — Refined Round 2: 500 Candidates, Code-Only Graphics

**Research baseline:** November 10, 2026 · **Scope:** iOS/iPadOS · **VisualCore path:** existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal · **Business:** one upfront purchase, no advertising, ad SDKs, IAP or subscriptions.

**Scope of evidence:** 500 ideas assessed, **not** 500 researched apps and **not** 500 prototypes. Exactly 200 concepts preserve the previous research matrix; 300 genuinely new concepts were written and scored against declared genre/technical priors. Numeric scores are screening judgments and are not forecasts, experimental results, consumer surveys or audited sales.

## Executive decision: launch a portfolio of experiments, not 25 clones

The screening examined **500** concepts across **62** explicit scoring criteria. **249** pass every proposed code-only/visual/gameplay gate (**20** from the original 200; **229** from the new 300). **25** enter a diverse portfolio shortlist (**4** inherited; **21** newly proposed). Scores favor genuine shader and procedural spectacle, but *a top-25 ranking is a decision to prototype, not a commitment to publish every candidate*.

### Hard requirements

- Graphics originate in procedural geometry, signed distance fields, GLSL ES, parametric meshes, instancing, particles, lighting, algorithms and simulation. There are **zero AI-generated images**, photographic background plates, manually sculpted characters, purchased level art or commissioned texture requirements.
- Use **only the existing VisualCore / projectM-iOS rendering bridge**, through the established ANGLE Metal backend. Do not replace ANGLE, recreate an independent Metal renderer, or ship different backends for each game.
- The visual effect must materially embody a decision in gameplay: steering, folding, redirecting, growing, balancing, tuning or routing. A screensaver with a score counter does not qualify.
- Every game is complete for an upfront $1.99–$4.99 purchase; no ads anywhere, ad SDKs, rewarded screens, analytics ad identifiers, microtransactions, subscriptions, user accounts or live-services infrastructure.
- All physics and visual render loops are bounded and deterministic enough for automation and adaptive quality on D3. This is an *engineering estimate* pending instrumented device tests.
- A portfolio release must satisfy Apple’s originality and spam guidance: no clones of existing games, and no two VisualCore offerings that differ only by visuals or theme. Similar ideas should be merged into a single substantial game.

## 1. Market evidence: what is known, and what is not

- **The mobile gaming market is huge, but not a premium-sales forecast.** Sensor Tower’s [State of Gaming 2026](https://sensortower.com/press/press-release-sensor-tower-state-of-gaming-gaming-drove-52-billion-downloads-82b-iap-revenue-on-mobile-and-12b-premium-revenue-on-steam) reports approximately **$82 billion of 2025 mobile game in-app-purchase revenue** and approximately 52 billion game downloads across mobile, PC and consoles. That $82 billion figure does not represent purchases of upfront-priced iOS games. Gaming downloads per minute are a global scale statistic, not a customer acquisition forecast.

- **People demonstrably pay upfront for some mobile games.** Apple’s [2025 U.S. iPhone top-paid list](https://apps.apple.com/us/iphone/room/6756363168) includes Minecraft, Balatro, Geometry Dash, Bloons TD 6, Stardew Valley, and other recognizable products. Those titles are unusually established competitors; no percentage can be inferred for unknown VisualCore games.

- **Premium, calm, visually distinctive desktop mechanics have audience evidence.** [Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/) and [Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/) have real positive Steam customer reviews; [Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/) demonstrates a minimalist routing loop; [Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/) shows demand for stylized art puzzles; [Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/) shows engagement with construction-physics systems. These are **genre precedents, not proposals to copy**.

- **PC platform context, not sales attribution.** The [October 2026 Steam hardware survey](https://store.steampowered.com/hwsurvey/) reported approximately **93.70% Windows, 3.95% Linux and 2.35% macOS** among respondents. A game working across Windows/macOS/Linux helps demonstrate broad design appeal, but these percentages are neither revenue shares nor iOS conversion metrics.

- **Steam visibility does not equal predictable money.** SteamDB’s [relaxing-game catalog](https://steamdb.info/tag/1654/?min_reviews=500) exposes relative review/follower/peak-player measures; pricing and review counts are public but unit sales cannot be inferred reliably by simply multiplying reviews by a constant. This portfolio therefore does not invent per-candidate sales numbers.

| Comparable PC product | Verified lesson | Porting caveat |
|---|---|---|
| [[Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/)] | Procedural diorama creation has strong positive reception; its official Steam store lists Windows, macOS and Linux requirements | Its rendering budgets, assets, controls and developer recognition do not automatically carry to iPhone |
| [[Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/)] | A small visual ruleset can deliver meaningful strategy without elaborate character animation | Its map-driven 2D interaction differs from three-dimensional spectacle |
| [[Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/)] | Geometry and systems can deliver relaxation with decision-making | Procedural 3D landscapes need device-level simplification |
| [[Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/)] | Art-led premium puzzles can accumulate a dedicated audience | A new 3D optics game must not mimic protected stained-glass motifs or arrangements |
| [[Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/)] | Physics construction can support complete, rule-driven play | A phone needs shorter stages, cheaper simulation and touch-first controls |

## 2. Copyright, App Store policy and the danger of indistinguishable games

The [U.S. Copyright Office](https://www.copyright.gov/register/tx-games.html) says that a game idea or playing method is not itself protected by copyright, but specific artwork, text and other expression can be. This is not a license to reuse game code, exact levels, names, trademarks, audio, distinctive visual identity or copied marketing. Open-source licenses must be audited if any source is considered, and no code from other games is required for the shortlisted titles.

Apple [App Review Guidelines 4.1 and 4.3](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) flag copycats and repeated near-identical apps. **The goal is not to flood the App Store with 25 shader reskins.** For every candidate the product team must document one mechanic, one content structure and one user experience that differs materially from every other shipped app; merge overlapping ideas when they do not pass the distinctiveness review.

## 3. All 62 criteria, rubric and score calculation

Each criterion is rated on a **1–5 ordinal judgment scale** (1 = weak, 3 = plausible, 5 = strong). Decimal ratings indicate heuristic prioritization, *not measured accuracy*. Original 200 candidates retain their earlier 50 and 12 ratings; 300 new concepts receive scores from their old-category reference averages plus documented text/trait modifiers (see the included code). No row has its own directly observed purchase conversion data.

**Commercial/engineering subtotal:** `C = 20 × Σ(criterion_rating × original_weight × group_multiplier) / Σ(original_weight × group_multiplier)`, with multipliers Market 0.78, Competition 0.86, Premium 1.00, Experience 1.22, Engineering 1.29.

**Visual subtotal:** `V = 20 × Σ(visual_rating × visual_weight) / Σ(visual_weight)`. **Final screening score:** `0.30 × C + 0.70 × V`. The 70% weighting prioritizes code-generatable spectacle. **Eligibility is assessed independently before shortlisting**; an unqualified game cannot win by a high weighted average.

## 6. Revenue economics without ads or in-app purchases

The only monetization event is buying the app. The following is simple arithmetic under assumed **15% or 30% platform fees**, ignoring taxes, refunds, localization, overhead, development labor and variable costs. Eligibility for any reduced fee is not assumed. These are **scenarios, not forecasts**.

| Price | Gross at 500 purchases | Net at 500 / 15% assumed | Net at 2,000 / 15% assumed | Net at 10,000 / 30% assumed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $1.99 | $995 | $846 | $3,383 | $13,930 |
| $2.99 | $1,495 | $1,271 | $5,083 | $20,930 |
| $3.99 | $1,995 | $1,696 | $6,783 | $27,930 |
| $4.99 | $2,495 | $2,121 | $8,483 | $34,930 |

**Go/no-go arithmetic:** At $3.99 and an illustrative 15% fee, each paid installation nets $3.3915 before refunds and taxes. Recovering a hypothetical $10,000 cash expense would require approximately 2,949 paid installations under those assumptions. This is not the expected number of buyers; it is a check on development scope. Human opportunity cost still matters even when Claude writes most code.

## 7. VisualCore architecture: code must create the art

```text
Claude Desktop → Swift/XcodeGen/SwiftPM + GLSL ES source
                         ↓
                  App-specific rule model
                         ↓
          VisualCore scene/mesh/material/FX APIs
                         ↓
              OpenGL ES 3.0 / EGL via ANGLE
                         ↓
                  Existing Metal backend
                         ↓
                 iPhone/iPad physical GPU
```

Keep owned `Vendor/projectM` and `Vendor/angle` forks pinned; do not delete the large ANGLE dependency checkout or place generated frameworks in a case-colliding folder. Procedural building blocks should include: `SDFPrimitives`, `MeshExtrusion`, `Instancing`, `SceneGraph`, `ColorScience`, `SoftLightApprox`, `ParticleBatch`, `RibbonRenderer`, `HeightfieldSim`, `FixedStepPhysics`, `OrbitMath`, `SeededLevelGenerator`, `VisualSnapshotHarness`, `GPUFrameTelemetry`, `AccessibleControlOverlay`. Names are proposed, not pre-existing audited APIs. Use feature negotiation; do not rely on unsupported GLES compute shaders or costly full volumetric raymarches.

### Low-cost ways to appear luxurious

- Use band-limited gradients, high-quality normals, disciplined emissive layers and restrained bloom as core shader styles. More passes do not automatically mean more beauty.
- Represent auroras, waves, light ribbons and fluid channels as tessellated spline strips with GLSL displacement rather than true high-cost volume simulation.
- Approximate refraction with normal-based color separation and screen-space cues; do not assert physically accurate caustics without a validated optical model.
- Batch instanced geometry and point sprites, pool particle buffers, cache compiled shader variants and preprocess parametric mesh topology.
- Prefer fixed-seed deterministic level and scene generation. Make gameplay physics stable across devices; rendering may choose dynamic resolution and particle caps.
- Test hero scenes without overlays, then at normal small-phone display scale including touch affordances, accessibility and visual comfort.
- Every app uses its own gameplay systems, progress structure, voice and product identity. Share engine code but do not ship repetitive templates.

## 8. Implementation and physical-device strategy

**Desktop-first full implementation:** Claude Code in the Claude Desktop application writes all game features, specs, code, unit tests, host and simulator UI tests. Do not invoke Claude CLI as a supervisor. Finish the entire set of chosen distinct app targets and freeze code before launching the official three-device testing campaign, as specified in the VisualCore master runbook. Machine commands may run through Desktop Code tasks.

**Recorded device matrix (verify live connection and OS version before testing):**

| Device | Hardware | Recorded OS | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | iPhone 15, iPhone15,4 | iOS 27.0.1 | iPhone interaction and frame pacing reference |
| D2 | iPad Pro 13-inch M5, iPad17,3 | iPadOS 27.2 | Large-screen scaling and high-end visual effects |
| D3 | iPad A16, iPad15,7 | iPadOS 26.5 | Oldest-performance tier, backward-compatibility proof; **never update** |

**Verification after implementation lock:** use `devicectl` with record-and-exit in-app automation runners, signed local builds, real `xcresult` bundles and structured per-seed render exports. Capture cold start, first frame, level success, touch misses, actual frame pacing, shader compilation hitches, GPU time, thermal state, visible image quality and crash-free operation. Target 60fps where feasible, with a documented 30fps quality mode if it meets player-quality criteria; do not convert any assumption into a “passed” badge. Run each game sequentially on D1 → D2 → D3, collect evidence and then fix, relock and rerun impacted suites. Never automate privileged device dialogs by bypassing Apple controls.

**Automated art acceptance:** a seed-camera matrix captures 10 hero views per game, validates no missing surfaces, NaNs, black frames, wrong aspect ratios or offscreen UI, then flags perceptual differences for a limited human quality audit. Automated image comparison alone cannot establish “stunning”; a minimal outside-player screenshot comprehension test must occur before launch, even if most code is AI-authored.

**Must-stop failures:** forced new art assets; unverified licensing; app looks flat despite numerical score; 10-second goal cannot be explained; D3 shader compilation stutters; significant heat; frequent crashes; visually indistinguishable portfolio members; market comparator too remote to support the business case.

## 9. Top 25: original product hypotheses and implementation sketches

### 01. Aurora Loom — 94.80 / 100

**Premise:** Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies.

**Visual hook, rendered in code:** Layered ribbon meshes with wave displacement and fragment interference patterns.

**Touch-first interaction:** Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification.

**Premium packaging:** $2.99 complete, offline and paid once. Estimated production scope: **10 person-weeks** is an initial heuristic, not a project estimate backed by benchmarking.

**Why it might win:** the player visibly sculpts the same live system that makes the screen extraordinary. `G162` reaches a visual score of 97.83/100 on conceptual screening, with all twelve code-only thresholds met.

**Market analog / competition:** [Glass Masquerade official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/); this is category-level evidence only. Also compare its moment-to-moment mechanic against other selected titles—especially Colorfall Canyons.

**Top risk:** thermal and overdraw risk on D3; crowding among optical/geometry premium games.

**Falsifiable vertical slice:** implement ten seeded frequency settings whose targets can be evaluated by a numeric tolerance; record whether the game is fun *without* the hero shader, and separately record whether the hero shader runs sustainably on D3.

**AssertionOutline:** see Section 01 in `Round-2-Top25-Complete-AssertionOutlines.md` for all three claims, twelve reasons, twelve evidence items, objections and stop conditions.

### 03. Wave Knot Keeper — 94.30 / 100

**Visual hook, rendered in code:** Parametric star volumes, glowing triangulation rays and projection-matched constellations.

**Touch-first interaction:** Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification.

**Premium packaging:** $3.99 complete, offline and paid once. Estimated production scope: **12 person-weeks** is an initial heuristic, not a project estimate backed by benchmarking.

**Why it might win:** the player visibly sculpts the same live system that makes the screen extraordinary. `G122` reaches a visual score of 96.05/100 on conceptual screening, with all twelve code-only thresholds met.

**Market analog / competition:** [Glass Masquerade official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/); this is category-level evidence only. Also compare its moment-to-moment mechanic against other selected titles—especially other geometry and visual puzzles.

**Top risk:** thermal and overdraw risk on D3.

**Falsifiable vertical slice:** implement ten replayable seeded levels with a deterministic solution checker and failure reason; record whether the game is fun *without* the hero shader, and separately record whether the hero shader runs sustainably on D3.

**AssertionOutline:** see Section 25 in `Round-2-Top25-Complete-AssertionOutlines.md` for all three claims, twelve reasons, twelve evidence items, objections and stop conditions.

## 11. Failure modes and the critical-thinking response

**A visual demo is not a game.** The required discriminator is a puzzle or simulation whose choices matter. If players enjoy watching but cannot describe a decision, move it to VisualCore demo gallery, not the $3.99 games catalog.

**A high score is not statistical prediction.** The 300 new candidates inherit category-specific priors and deterministic semantic adjustments. The earlier 200 use different, historically assessed hand-tuned judgments; this is *transparent but not blinded or independently calibrated*. Do not infer that new-vs-old rank differences are evidence of demand.

**The source landscape is not exhaustive.** The current study reviews a handful of influential PC titles and published top-paid charts, not every competitor in the App Store. Commission an exact keyword/name/trademark search and test competitor gameplay before final decisions.

**Technology scope risk.** ANGLE's iOS Metal support does not establish fast blur, transparency or signed-distance traversal on D3. Build efficient approximations and measure shader translation and pipeline compilation; preserve Xcode and ANGLE fork reproducibility.

**Visual similarity within the portfolio.** This is a real product and App Review threat. Prototype in themed waves; if two games feel interchangeable, merge mechanics into one richer app rather than releasing both.

**Paid market cost.** A no-ad strategy is a product quality choice, not evidence that organic discovery is free. Invest in genuine trailers captured from the real renderer, screenshots, player research, reviews and community participation—not promotional ad networks.

## 12. Final recommendation: build only what the evidence earns

**First three technical prototypes:** Aurora Loom for spectacular ribbon/color shader fundamentals; Lissajous Labyrinth for deterministic math-driven gameplay; Wave Knot Keeper for spatial depth and topology interaction. **But do not ship all three as separate apps before proving distinct mechanics**, because their visual language overlaps. A more diversified trial might use Aurora Loom, Echo Cartographer and Voxel Origami for different kinds of interaction.

**Two-stage proof:** (1) code-only complete playable vertical slices with simulator acceptance, distinctive art and a standalone paid-game loop; (2) after portfolio-wide implementation lock, D1/D2/D3 stress evidence and a small real-player comprehension test. Only then select release waves. This separates engineering possibility from actual customer appetite.

## 11. Round completion audit and next-round unlock
**This round unlocks `round6.md` only if every one of the 25 new games has (a) all ten x eight Spec Kit stages, (b) zero missing source/solver/level artifacts, (c) clean relevant simulator runs, (d) signed lock source SHA and explicit 75 physical device outcomes from D1/D2/D3 (genuine PASS or documented non-passing blockers that cannot claim complete), (e) shared F12 convergence with no unreviewed issue, (f) no ads/IAP/art SDKs and (g) unique-product audit.** A failure remains incomplete rather than misrepresented; a following round is forbidden until complete or a transparent owner-approved scope amendment with dated explanation.
**File integrity:** check this Markdown size and SHA-256, the roster count/unique source IDs, exactly 12 shared and 250 game feature IDs, eight command prompts each, 25×3×4 argument entries, 100 content slots per game, 80 scenario rows per game and no duplicate candidate names across rounds. Mark published references time-bounded and avoid inventing runtime facts. D3 must remain on 26.5.
